title: Events, commands, queues, and a retained log
outcome: Choose messaging from responsibility, history, replay, and timing needs.
useCase: Choosing a messaging model for reports and ticket facts.
benefits: Clear responsibility and justified asynchronous boundaries.
drawbacks: Async systems need duplicate, delay, schema, and recovery handling.
version: Kafka 4.1 KRaft · lab Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 · legacy Rails adaptation notes
cue: Command asks. Event tells. Log remembers under a policy.

trace.title: Business decision
trace.detail: A command asks someone to do something: GenerateReport. An event states a fact: TicketCompleted. Naming the difference helps decide who owns rejection, completion, and follow-up work.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Business decision commits → fact is published → independent subscribers process later → their results become visible. Ask where a user can check each outcome and how old work may be replayed.

Compare one reporting group with three workers versus two independent groups. Worker count and subscriber responsibility are different axes.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Changing a direct call into an event does not make the effect immediate or atomic. A queue/log is not the application’s permission authority.
